summary: Iron oxide and magnesium oxide thin films were deposited using ferrocene, (dimethylaminomethyl)ferrocene, magnesium β-diketonate, and ozone via atomic layer deposition. The phase composition of the films was influenced by the deposition temperature, with magnetite and maghemite forming at lower temperatures. The study aimed to investigate the effects of deposition temperature and MgO doping on the phase composition and magnetization of the films.
evidence: Iron oxide and magnesium-doped iron oxide films were grown by atomic layer deposition in the temperature range of 350–500 ◦C from ferrocene, (dimethylaminomethyl)ferrocene, magnesium β-diketonate, and ozone. The aim of the study was the investigation of the effects of deposition temperature and MgO-doping on the phase composition and magnetization of the iron oxide based films.
